summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat's Robert L. Burnes finished his weekend story on Tom Allen, writing that Allen quit boxing over the Queensberry rules, that his estate came to $278.35, and that his great-grandson holds his silver cup.

metadata.notes: Page header reads '2C St. Louis Globe-Democrat Tues. Apr. 4, 1978'.

facts.fact: Allen retired rather than fight under the Queensberry rules with gloves
facts.quote: They've made it a sissy sport. I want no part of it.

facts.fact: Allen's daughter Mary, also called Polly, came to the United States with him and married Edward Taylor of St. Louis
Allen's will left everything to his daughter Polly Allen Taylor and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove
When Allen's will was probated, the estate amounted to $278.35
Allen's silver cup went to Tillie Hartgrove after his death; it was later retrieved from a Market Street pawn shop in 1938 by the father of great-grandson Thomas Allen Taylor
A family story held that Allen owned a diamond belt for the world championship, but no one could verify it

notes: The 'sissy sport' quote is reported 75 years after the fact without a source, hence low confidence. Thomas Allen Taylor planned to offer the cup to the Missouri Historical Society (1978), not added as a fact.
